clue.text: See 31
First person to be professional driver, after car sweets

indicators.note: after says the car piece comes first, ahead of the other two

parts.note: taken as written
'I am' is the first person singular of the verb to be
Ernie Els is a professional golfer, and a golfer drives the ball

explanation.surface: A chauffeur's first job is said to come after the car's own treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after car' puts CAR at the front. A driver is also a golf club, so the 'professional driver' is the South African golfer Ernie Els.
explanation.definitionFit: Small chewy toffees made from boiled sugar and butter are a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Second half of some freak's short list

indicators.note: the second half of the four-letter word some is its last two letters
short says the word for freak loses its last letter

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic or freak, as in 'a fitness nut'

explanation.surface: A list of an oddball's foibles has been cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare is a list of the dishes available.

clue.text: Conceals kinky sex with rest

parts.note: SM is short for sadomasochism, a kinky sexual practice
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Someone hides their kinky sexual habits along with everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it up or suppress it, so smothers is a synonym of hides.

clue.text: Doctor right about fungal disease

indicators.note: about says the word for right is turned round, read back to front

parts.note: a Tory is a right-wing Conservative in British politics

explanation.surface: A physician correctly diagnoses a fungal infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' suggests the opposite of wrong, but here it means the political right: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that decays timber, a disease of wood in buildings.

clue.text: Essentially, it's not about odd man — Charlie and the Chocolate Factory's musical song

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letter is taken from each word that follows

explanation.surface: A tribute to the Roald Dahl musical about a boy and a sweet factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the centre letter of each of the ten words from 'it's' to 'Factory's'. The song is from Cole Porter's musical Kiss Me, Kate, not from the Dahl show the surface names.
explanation.definitionFit: A number from Cole Porter's stage show Kiss Me, Kate, so a song from a musical.

clue.text: Rewriting Roald Dahl's final piece for money

indicators.note: rewriting the letters of the name and the extra letter puts them in a new order
the final piece of the author's surname is its last letter

explanation.surface: An editor reworks the end of a Roald Dahl story in return for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is the currency unit of the US and other countries, so it stands for money.

clue.text: Spoiled Violet Beauregarde's hollow sign of affection

indicators.note: Violet in the story is a spoiled child, but here the word says her name's letters are mixed up
hollow says the surname is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: The spoiled girl from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory leaves an empty mark of fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Beauregarde is the gum-chewing girl in Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. 'Spoiled' describes her character but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hickey left on the skin by a kiss or nip is a mark of fondness between lovers.

clue.text: The first prize, it's mad

parts.note: the first is number one, I in Roman numerals
to prize something is to rate or value it highly

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about who won the top award.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of angry or furious, not in the sense of insane.

clue.text: Chocolate bar shortened by company sweet discoverer

indicators.note: shortened says the bar's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a Mars bar is a well-known chocolate bar
Polo is a brand of mint sweet with a hole in the middle

explanation.surface: A confectionery firm cuts the size of its chocolate bar and finds a new sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars and Polo are British confectionery brands: a chocolate bar and a ring-shaped mint.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian traveller who reached China and described it for Europeans is called an explorer or discoverer.

clue.text: Veruca Salt's second to upset one discharging

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the gathered words are knocked into a new order
second picks the second letter of the surname that follows

explanation.surface: The bratty Veruca Salt from the Chocolate Factory story is about to throw a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: Veruca Salt is the spoilt girl in Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. Her first name, the A of Salt and TO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that empties or clears out a space is an evacuator, one discharging its contents.

clue.text: Sweet chap's beginning to hand out bags

indicators.note: bags here means grabs and holds, so one piece is put around the other

parts.note: to dole is to hand out or distribute

indicators.note: the beginning of the word chap is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man starts giving out bags of sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for sweet, used as a musical direction to play softly and sweetly.

clue.text: Queen to copy her speech rejected draft

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
to ape is to copy or imitate
RP, Received Pronunciation, is the Queen's English, her way of speaking

explanation.surface: Her Majesty's speech draft was copied and then turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses the whole of ER + APE + RP (ERAPERP). RP is Received Pronunciation, the prestige British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft something is to draw up or get it ready, a verb meaning make ready.

clue.text: Place a 10-point tile on a square

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in street names
in Scrabble the Z tile scores ten points

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player puts the high-scoring tile on a square of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like part of the Scrabble board but is the definition: a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style public square or open marketplace in a town.

clue.text: Like great food, no starter's great

indicators.note: no starter means the word loses its first letter, like a meal without its first course

parts.note: gastronomic describes fine cooking and eating

explanation.surface: A gourmet says a meal without a first course is still wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic means enormous, huge, as in astronomic prices: great in size.

clue.text: Bullfighters ruptured, got up, finishing early

parts.note: tore means ripped or ruptured

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: rose means got up out of bed

explanation.surface: A matador's injuries sound like he was gored and left early.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish bullfighters on foot, a general word for those in the ring.

clue.text: So work interrupted by Charlie Bucket

indicators.note: interrupted by means the letter breaks into the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Charlie Bucket from Dahl's story breaks off from his labours.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Bucket is the hero of the Dahl book, but here 'Bucket' is the definition, a scoop for lifting things.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is a deep ladle or shovel, a small container for lifting things, like a pail.

clue.text: Film on Charlie's prized possession

indicators.note: on means placed after, as in an across clue a piece sits on what it follows

parts.note: a charlie is a fool, an ass, in British slang
ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A movie is the treasured belonging of someone named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a right charlie' is British for a fool, so Charlie is ASS, not C or Chaplin.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something valuable that one owns, a prized belonging.

clue.text: So chapter is over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read back to front

explanation.surface: Thus the chapter is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for thus, printed after a quoted mistake to show it is reproduced as written.

clue.text: Most blue, Charlie's in bed

indicators.note: in means the fool's letters go inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a charlie is a fool, an arse in British slang; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Charlie is tucked up in bed feeling deeply sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests sadness but means smutty. A charlie and an arse are both British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means rude or vulgar, as in blue jokes, so most blue is the crudest.

clue.text: Animal in river?

parts.note: the creature's full name comes from Greek for river horse, and it lives in rivers

explanation.definitionFit: A short name for the large African mammal whose Greek name means horse of the river.

clue.text: Quiet about sex, if turning up as Mr and Mrs?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple keep their love life quiet if they are wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr and Mrs' suggests a married couple and 'sex' a bedroom secret, but the titles are things placed before names.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles such as these come before a name, the way word parts are attached at the start.

clue.text: Fudge leads to young Augustus Gloop saying sorry

indicators.note: to fudge is to fiddle or fake, so the letters are rearranged
the leads of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The greedy boy Augustus Gloop apologises after leading young ones to the fudge.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus Gloop is the greedy boy in Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. 'Fudge' looks like a sweet but is the anagram signal for Y, A and GLOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology is an expression of regret, the act of making amends in words.

clue.text: They hold winner, hiding in large packaging

indicators.note: packaging means the size letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing size label for large

indicators.note: hiding means the word for the preposition is put out of sight, taken out

explanation.surface: Champions are concealed inside a big box.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label for large; 'hiding' removes the clue's own word 'in' from the word for champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Owners are those who hold or possess property, so they hold things.

clue.text: Endlessly spoke Willy Wonka's last parts, actor recalled

indicators.note: the last parts of the two names are their final letters
recalled means called back, so the surname is reversed

parts.note: Johnny Depp played Willy Wonka in the 2005 film

explanation.surface: The film star who played Willy Wonka nattered on about his final scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses DEPP to PPED. Johnny Depp played Wonka in Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (2005).
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to talk at length in a shrill, irritating way, so to chatter on and on.

clue.text: Mostly with Charlie in European city

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: and means together with
a charlie is a fool, a twerp, in British slang

explanation.surface: Charlie spends most of his time in a continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium, in northern Europe.

clue.text: Got it in mouth back to front!

indicators.note: back to front says the last letter at the back is brought round to the front

parts.note: taken as written
gob is British slang for mouth

explanation.surface: Someone shouts that they have it in their mouth the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the B at the end of INGOB to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of triumph on finding or completing something, like eureka.

clue.text: See 8
Those that follow notice chosen child in playground yard

parts.note: a poster is a public notice
in the game of tag, the chaser is called it

explanation.surface: A sign in a school yard picks out a particular pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: In playground tag the child who chases is 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterity means future generations, the people who come after.

clue.text: English books section declines

parts.note: B stands for book, so two of them give books

explanation.surface: A part of the English books shelf is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it goes out, so to ebb is to decline or wane.

clue.text: Peasant's left out of frame featuring Buckets?

indicators.note: left out means the letter for left is removed

parts.note: a yokel is a country bumpkin or peasant

explanation.surface: A country fellow is left out of the Bucket family portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from YOKEL. The Buckets are Charlie's family; here they are buckets carried on a yoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden crosspiece laid over the shoulders, used to carry a pail at each end.

clue.text: Doctor's transport contracts head for delay

indicators.note: contracts means shrinks, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the TARDIS is the time machine of Doctor Who
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: The Doctor's time machine shrinks its leading end and holds things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the time machine in the BBC's Doctor Who, and a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness, the state of being behind time.

clue.text: Bar and Mike Teavee's wrapper go around 11?

indicators.note: go around means the gathered letters circulate into a new order
the wrapper of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A chocolate bar and Mike Teavee's wrapper are passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Teavee is the TV-obsessed boy in Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. '11' looks like a cross-reference to 11 across but is the time eleven o'clock, a mid-morning pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven in the morning is a common time for a short rest from work, as with elevenses.
